selectionNote: Curated illustrative cases, expanded November 16, 2026; not a representative sample or a success-rate denominator. Organization-reported claims, field experiments, regulator outcomes and studies are distinguished.

cases.title: 70 years of engineering drawings, searchable in minutes
cases.summary: Engineers search decades of historical drawings for replacement parts. The company reports that searches fell from almost an hour to 4.5 minutes.
cases.evidence: A projected 90% annual reduction in drawing-search hours is a forecast, not a measured annual result.
cases.risk: Wrong drawings or model mismatches could create equipment and safety risks. Engineering verification is necessary.
cases.apply: Test retrieval accuracy on 30 known drawing-lookup questions before estimating savings.
cases.question: What should engineers verify before acting on an AI-retrieved drawing?

cases.title: Agentic software development and AI code review
cases.summary: The company reports shipping roughly 20 times more software with the same engineering team using coding agents and AI-assisted review.
cases.evidence: Self-reported output does not independently prove 20 times the delivered value or quality.
cases.risk: More code can increase security defects, testing bottlenecks and maintenance.
cases.apply: Measure completed tested changes and defect rates, not AI-generated lines of code.
cases.question: Does producing 20 times more code mean producing 20 times more value?

cases.title: Employee AI pilot with claimed strong ROI
cases.summary: A 315-person enterprise AI pilot reported approximately 14 hours saved per participant monthly; broader rollout followed.
cases.evidence: ROI and savings are pilot estimates in a vendor case study, not independently audited enterprise-wide results.
cases.risk: Self-reported time savings may not translate into actual cash savings. Confidentiality and employee data require controls.
cases.apply: Compare a narrow repetitive workflow before and after AI with quality and time measures.
cases.question: What evidence would you require before accepting a 954% ROI claim?

cases.title: AI-powered service assistants and faster resolutions
cases.summary: Google Cloud reports that Best Buy increased call containment by more than 50%, with fewer transfers between service agents.
cases.evidence: Figures are supplier-reported and do not independently establish causal impact or customer satisfaction.
cases.risk: Containment can rise without problems getting resolved; satisfaction and escalation matter.
cases.apply: Test a narrow FAQ workflow with resolution, transfer, and satisfaction measures.
cases.question: If fewer calls reach people, how do we know customers are better served?

cases.title: Advisor knowledge assistant and meeting summaries
cases.summary: Advisors use internal AI tools for retrieving firm information and preparing meeting notes and follow-up drafts.
cases.evidence: Adoption is reported by the company and vendor; it does not itself establish ROI.
cases.risk: Confidentiality, inaccuracies and meeting consent require strict controls and human review.
cases.apply: Evaluate citation accuracy against an approved knowledge base before increasing use.
cases.question: Why might retrieval evaluations matter more than a model name?

cases.title: Customer service automation with human support retained
cases.summary: Klarna says its AI assistant handled 80% of customer-service chats in 2025 while human support remained available.
cases.evidence: The figure appears in an SEC filing; it is not a customer satisfaction metric or a count of jobs eliminated.
cases.risk: Sensitive financial questions may require accessible human escalation and repeat-contact monitoring.
cases.apply: Measure complaints, repeat contacts, transfers, quality and full service cost alongside automation rate.
cases.question: Why is AI chat share not itself a success rate?

cases.title: Public-service chatbot accuracy problems and discontinuation
cases.summary: An NYC audit identified inaccurate and inconsistent chatbot guidance and oversight problems; an official report records decommissioning in February 2026.
cases.evidence: Independent government audit plus separate official disclosure document establish the reported findings and shutdown.
cases.risk: Inaccurate guidance about legal or regulatory requirements can result in consequential harm.
cases.apply: Constrain high-stakes responses to verified sources, test consistency and ensure escalation.
cases.question: Should public-service bots be launched before independent accuracy testing?

cases.title: Incorrect chatbot refund advice led to liability
cases.summary: A customer relied on inaccurate automated bereavement-fare advice. A British Columbia tribunal found Air Canada responsible.
cases.evidence: The tribunal confirmed the award but did not establish the chatbot's model or whether it used generative AI.
cases.risk: Automated policy responses can mislead customers and organizations remain accountable.
cases.apply: Audit automated guidance against official policy and provide escalation and corrections.
cases.question: Who bears responsibility when a business chatbot gives wrong information?

cases.title: AI tools support frontline store associates
cases.summary: Walmart announced AI-powered tools in its associate app for task management and translation, with a reported reduction in shift-planning time.
cases.evidence: Walmart's announcement describes company-reported operational improvements and a rollout; the announcement does not establish an independently audited causal estimate or outcomes at every store.
cases.risk: Frontline systems must work for workers with varying languages, access and technical skills; outputs need supervision.
cases.apply: Pilot AI support on one repeatable store-management task, checking time savings and worker experience.
cases.question: How would you test whether this tool genuinely helps associates rather than shifting work onto them?

cases.title: LLM Suite reaches a large internal employee base
cases.metric_label: Employees onboarded in first eight months, company reported
cases.summary: JPMorganChase launched an internal generative AI environment to support drafting, ideation and access to AI capabilities under enterprise controls.
cases.evidence: The company reports 200,000 onboarded users in eight months, which shows scale of onboarding rather than independently demonstrating time savings, adoption depth or financial ROI.
cases.risk: Large-scale internal AI needs safeguards for sensitive financial data, model errors and employee training.
cases.apply: Measure adoption, usefulness and error rates separately before attributing business value to user counts.
cases.question: What is the difference between 200,000 people onboarded and 200,000 people achieving measurable value?

cases.title: Ambient AI notes bring modest documentation gains
cases.metric_label: Change in time per note in first month, study estimate
cases.summary: A peer-reviewed observational study examined ambient AI documentation across a large health system and found modest reductions in time spent on notes, with other outcomes varying.
cases.evidence: The JAMA Network Open study included 1,547 clinicians and reported a 0.26-minute first-month reduction in mean note time; it was not randomized and did not show more appointments per day.
cases.risk: AI-generated clinical notes may contain omissions or errors and require clinician review; modest efficiency improvements should not be overstated.
cases.apply: Test documentation tools on time, note quality, clinician burden and patient safety rather than relying on a single time metric.
cases.question: Why might a statistically significant time difference still have limited practical value?

cases.title: AI drive-through ordering pilot ends without scale-up
cases.summary: McDonald's ended its AI-powered drive-through ordering test with IBM after operating a limited pilot rather than scaling that system to all restaurants.
cases.evidence: McDonald's confirmed ending the IBM automated-order-taker test. Public reports described errors, but the evidence does not establish a precise failure rate or that all automated voice ordering is unworkable.
cases.risk: Noisy environments, accents, order complexity and mistakes can damage customer experience and increase rework.
cases.apply: Use an actual drive-through pilot to measure order accuracy, staff intervention, speed and customer trust.
cases.question: What pilot results would convince you to expand—or stop—an AI ordering system?

cases.title: Automated hiring screening triggers age-discrimination settlement
cases.summary: The U.S. EEOC reported that iTutorGroup agreed to pay $365,000 to settle charges that its automated application screening rejected more than 200 older applicants.
cases.evidence: The EEOC alleges the software was programmed to reject applicants by age; the case ended in a settlement, not a court verdict following a trial. Whether the system used generative AI is not established.
cases.risk: Automated screening can systematically exclude protected groups; human oversight and discrimination tests are essential.
cases.apply: Audit rejection rules by protected-group impact, test with counterfactual profiles, and allow appeals before deployment.
cases.question: How could an automated system discriminate even if its creators never used generative AI?

cases.title: Randomized experiments find developer productivity gains
cases.metric_label: Estimated increase in completed tasks across three field trials
cases.summary: Researchers combined three randomized field experiments involving 4,867 developers given access to an AI coding assistant, finding more completed tasks on average.
cases.evidence: Across three field experiments the pooled productivity estimate was 26.08% with standard error 10.3%. This is a task-completion measure, not a direct measure of customer value, defect rates, or all developers.
cases.risk: Faster task completion can still produce defects, security issues or additional review burdens.
cases.apply: Run a randomized team experiment measuring completed, tested work alongside quality and rework.
cases.question: What additional measures would tell you whether the 26% productivity estimate creates business value?

cases.title: AI assistance improves issue resolution, unevenly
cases.metric_label: Average issues resolved per hour across 5,172 agents
cases.summary: A peer-reviewed study of customer-support agents found AI assistance increased issues resolved per hour on average, with larger gains for less experienced agents.
cases.evidence: The Quarterly Journal of Economics study reported a 15% mean productivity improvement across 5,172 agents; effects differed by worker experience, and some highly skilled workers experienced small output-quality declines.
cases.risk: Average effects hide differences by role and experience; guidance can be unsuitable for complex customer problems.
cases.apply: Measure productivity and service quality by experience level and issue type, not only one overall average.
cases.question: If AI helps newer workers most, how should an organization redesign onboarding and coaching?

cases.title: AI-first workplace policy prompts public backlash and revision
cases.metric_label: Year CEO discussed policy lessons publicly
cases.summary: Duolingo's public AI-first policy triggered customer and workforce backlash; its CEO later discussed communication mistakes and limits of AI-generated work.
cases.evidence: The documented controversy concerns AI adoption policy and organizational communication, not a measured failure of Duolingo's language-teaching outcomes. Reports say the company withdrew AI-use scoring from performance reviews.
cases.risk: Poorly communicated automation mandates can undermine employee and customer trust even when some workflows benefit.
cases.apply: Explain what AI changes for workers, allow exceptions, and measure outcomes instead of mandating AI usage counts.
cases.question: What should leaders communicate before introducing an AI-first operating policy?
